report: The rapidly growing painless scrotal swelling initially suggested malignancy, but histopathology showing bland tall columnar mesothelial cells with WT-1+/ER+/PR+, calretinin−/D2-40− and no invasion or papillary growth is definitive for a benign mesothelial lesion. Imaging revealing a multilocular cystic lesion without solid components or enhancement further supports this diagnosis. These findings refute scrotal malignancy, hematocele, infection/inflammation, and trauma. Therefore, the evidence converges on a scrotal benign multicystic mesothelial lesion, most consistent with multilocular peritoneal inclusion cyst or cystadenoma.
